To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the set of all feasible contact states that can occur during an assembly operation is efficiently generated as a graph (Assembly Contact State Graph) that contains all possible contact states and indicates their neighbor relationships.

(i) the set of geometrically feasible contact state combinations can be efficiently represented by a directed graph, referred to here as the Assembly Contact State Graph; and (ii) an Assembly Contact State graph can be efficiently constructed by evaluating the geometric feasibility of the primitive principle contacts and the various combinations of principle contacts.

(1) a graph representation of feasible contacts can be used to represent the set of feasible contact states for assembly applications, and (2) a method has been developed that allows for efficient construction of such a graph, given a bounded set of possible misalignments.
